+///    alternate screen is excluded, TUI suppression is automatic and needs no code.
+///
+/// Writes its findings to files under the temp directory so the run needs no UI driving.

+  static let marker = "SPIKE-REPLAY-MARKER-7F3A"
+  static let primaryMarker = "SPIKE-PRIMARY-LINE-B21C"
+  static let altMarker = "SPIKE-ALTSCREEN-D904"
+
+  /// Application Support, not the temp dir: the session store already proves the app can write
+  /// there, and a sandbox container would redirect NSTemporaryDirectory somewhere hard to find.
+  static var outputDirectory: URL {

+      .appendingPathComponent("Workroom", isDirectory: true)
+      .appendingPathComponent("scrollback-spike", isDirectory: true)
+  }
+
+  private static func write(_ name: String, _ contents: String) {
+    let dir = outputDirectory
+    try? FileManager.default.createDirectory(at: dir, withIntermediateDirectories: true)
+    try? contents.write(
+      to: dir.appendingPathComponent(name), atomically: true, encoding: .utf8)
+  }
+
+  /// Drive the whole sequence off one surface. Times are generous — this is a one-shot probe, not a
+  /// test that has to be fast.
+  static func run(on view: GhosttySurfaceView) {
+    // Q1: replay bytes into an EXEC surface immediately after creation.
+    let replay = "\(marker)\r\n── restored session ──\r\n"
+    view.spikeWriteBuffer(replay)
+    write("00-attempted.txt", "wrote \(replay.utf8.count) bytes via write_buffer\n")
+
+    // Q1 readback: did those bytes reach the screen, and is the shell still alive?
+    schedule(2) {
+      let text = view.readFullSurface() ?? "<nil>"
+      write(
+        "01-after-replay.txt",
+        """
+        containsMarker=\(text.contains(marker))
+        length=\(text.count)
+        ---
+        \(text)
+        """)
+      // Produce known PRIMARY-screen content, proving the shell still works after the injection.
+      view.spikeSendLine("printf '\(primaryMarker)\\n'")
+    }
+
+    // Q2: enter the alternate screen and read while it is active.
+    schedule(5) {
+      let text = view.readFullSurface() ?? "<nil>"
+      write(
+        "02-after-primary.txt",
+        """
+        containsMarker=\(text.contains(marker))
+        containsPrimary=\(text.contains(primaryMarker))
+        ---
+        \(text)
+        """)
+      view.spikeSendLine(
+        "tput smcup; echo \(altMarker); sleep 12; tput rmcup")
+    }
+
+    schedule(9) {
+      let text = view.readFullSurface() ?? "<nil>"
+      write(
+        "03-during-altscreen.txt",
+        """
+        containsAlt=\(text.contains(altMarker))
+        containsPrimary=\(text.contains(primaryMarker))
+        containsMarker=\(text.contains(marker))
+        ---
+        \(text)
+        """)
+    }
+
+    schedule(24) {
+      let text = view.readFullSurface() ?? "<nil>"
+      write(
+        "04-after-altscreen-exit.txt",
+        """
+        containsAlt=\(text.contains(altMarker))
+        containsPrimary=\(text.contains(primaryMarker))
+        containsMarker=\(text.contains(marker))
+        ---
+        \(text)
+        """)
+      write("99-done.txt", "spike complete\n")
+    }
+  }
+
+  private static func schedule(_ seconds: TimeInterval, _ body: @escaping () -> Void) {
+    DispatchQueue.main.asyncAfter(deadline: .now() + seconds) {
+      MainActor.assumeIsolated(body)
+    }
+  }
+}
+
+extension ScrollbackSpike {
+  /// Unconditional breadcrumb so a silent run can be told apart from a flag that never read true.
+  static func note(_ message: String) {
+    let dir = outputDirectory
+    try? FileManager.default.createDirectory(at: dir, withIntermediateDirectories: true)
+    let url = dir.appendingPathComponent("_trace.txt")
+    let line = "\(Date()): \(message)\n"
+    if let handle = try? FileHandle(forWritingTo: url) {
+      handle.seekToEndOfFile()
+      handle.write(Data(line.utf8))
+      try? handle.close()
+    } else {
+      try? line.write(to: url, atomically: true, encoding: .utf8)
+    }
+  }

+      _ = XCTWaiter().wait(for: [expectation(description: "tick")], timeout: 1)

472	  /// Force a deterministic **UI** state in fixture mode: the inspector open, parked on
473	  /// `inspectorSection` with every section expanded, and the diff viewer in `diffViewMode`. Must be
474	  /// called before any `AppStore` is built (`WorkroomApp.init`), because `activeInspectorSection` and
475	  /// the layout both seed themselves from `Defaults` at construction.
476	  ///
477	  /// These are all `Defaults` keys in the app's real (Dev) UserDefaults domain, so without this a
478	  /// test inherits whatever the developer last left behind. That is not hypothetical: a collapsed
479	  /// section renders only its header, a closed inspector has nothing at all, and a `Dev`
480	  /// domain holding `diffViewMode = sideBySide` turned three `DiffViewerUITests` + two
481	  /// `DiffHighlightUITests` red for weeks — they assert on `diff.line`, which only the *unified*
482	  /// renderer emits, and read "the global default" from a pref the developer can change in Settings.
483	  ///
484	  /// The cost of pinning is that a fixture launch **overwrites** these keys in the Dev domain (it
485	  /// can't be a plain read: the views take them from `Defaults`). Dev is its own domain, so this
486	  /// never touches the release app's preferences — but a UI-test run does reset the Dev app's
487	  /// inspector and diff-mode choices, which is the deliberate trade for hermetic tests.
488	  ///
489	  /// A launch argument can't do this job. Argument-domain values arrive as **strings**
490	  /// (`-showNotificationsInspector 1` stores `"1"`, not `true`), and `Defaults` reads a natively
491	  /// supported type with `as? Bool`, which fails on a string and hands back the key's default
492	  /// (`false`) — so the argument doesn't just fail to force the pane open, it *pins it shut*: the
493	  /// argument domain outranks the app domain, so it also shadows the persisted value AND every
494	  /// later write (`AppStore.apply(.iconClick)`), leaving the pane unopenable for the whole run.
495	  /// `UITestFixture`'s own flags survive that only because `UserDefaults.bool(forKey:)` coerces
496	  /// strings. Hence a fixture-namespaced argument mirrored into `Defaults` here instead.
497	  ///
498	  /// `active` is a parameter, defaulting to the real flag, purely so its unit tests never have to
499	  /// WRITE `WorkroomUITestFixture`. Around 47 production sites branch on that key, including
500	  /// `AppStore.handleRootBranchChange`'s `guard !UITestFixture.isActive`, and `-parallel-testing`
501	  /// workers are separate processes sharing one on-disk defaults domain — so a class holding the key
502	  /// true for the length of a test body silently early-returns another class's history refresh, in a
503	  /// worker whose diff has nothing to do with any of this. That is the same cross-worker hazard
504	  /// `AppStore.confirmOnCloseOverrideForTesting` exists for; passing the state in avoids it at the
505	  /// source instead of racing and cleaning up.
506	  static func applyFixtureDefaults(active: Bool = isActive) {
507	    guard active else { return }
508	    Defaults[.showInspector] = true
509	    Defaults[.activeInspectorSection] = inspectorSection
510	    Defaults[.diffViewMode] = diffViewMode
511	    // Every section expanded, equal heights. Not optional book-keeping: collapse state decides whether
512	    // a section's BODY renders at all (a collapsed section keeps only its header), and it's global +
513	    // persisted, so without this a test inherits whichever sections the developer — or the last UI test
514	    // to press ⌥⌘C/⌥⌘Y — left shut, and reads as "the panel is broken".
515	    Defaults[.inspectorLayout] = .default
516	    // Workroom's own last-fetch stamps, for the same reason as the collapse state: they PERSIST, and a
517	    // fetch performed by an earlier test writes one. `RemoteStateModel` takes the later of the backend's
518	    // evidence and this stamp, so a leftover value silently overrode a seeded `.never` and the
519	    // never-fetched state reported "just now" instead.
520	    Defaults[.vcsLastFetch] = [:]
521	    // The theme family, for the same reason as the collapse state and the fetch stamps: it PERSISTS.
522	    // Without this a theme test inherits whatever the developer last picked, and a test that applies
523	    // a theme leaves it applied for the next run.
524	    Defaults[.themeFamily] = themeFamily
525	  }

728	  /// A deterministic canned diff for the diff viewer in fixture mode — so the UI tests render a real
729	  /// `DiffViewer` without shelling out to git/jj against the fake temp directory. The content encodes
730	  /// the file path and the `DiffSource` (git worktree / jj `@` / jj `@-`) so a test can assert it
731	  /// opened the *right* file's diff from the *right* revision. Two paths get special states for
732	  /// coverage: `binary.bin` → binary, `clean.txt` → empty.
733	  ///
734	  /// Ruby files get a diff whose new-side lines are exactly `rubyFileContent(for:)` (a small Ruby
735	  /// snippet), so the real highlight pipeline (detect → parse → map) runs against canned content and
736	  /// the syntax-highlight UI test can assert colour was applied. The tag line is a Ruby comment, so
737	  /// the existing revision-tag assertions still hold. Non-Ruby paths keep a generic diff with no
738	  /// matching content, so they exercise the plain (highlight-skipped) fallback.
739	  static func diff(for descriptor: DiffDescriptor) -> DiffResult {
740	    let name = (descriptor.path as NSString).lastPathComponent
741	    if name == "binary.bin" { return .binary }
742	    if name == "clean.txt" { return .empty }
743	    let tag = sourceTag(descriptor.source)
744	    if SyntaxLanguage.grammar(forPath: descriptor.path) == .ruby {
745	      return .diff(UnifiedDiff.parse(rubyDiffText(tag: tag, path: descriptor.path)))
746	    }
747	    let raw = """
748	      diff --git a/\(descriptor.path) b/\(descriptor.path)
749	      @@ -1,4 +1,5 @@
750	       context line one
751	      -removed old line
752	      +added line for \(tag)
753	      +marker \(descriptor.path)
754	       context line two
755	       context line three
756	      """
757	    return .diff(UnifiedDiff.parse(raw))
758	  }
